$comment: The weighted-₹ parity table (WS-26g, specs/crm_app.md §9 'WS-26g' block 1).
ONE file, read by BOTH runners: tests/unit/test_crm_reports.py drives it
through the emitted SQL (gateway/routes/crm/core.py::WEIGHTED_SQL, read out
of the statement text by tests/unit/_crm_fakes.py::_WEIGHTED_SUM_RE), and
board.ts::weightedDeal / weightedRows. Two independently typed tables are
not parity — that is the whole reason this file exists rather than a
comment pointing one implementation at the other.
A row is (amount, deal_probability, stage_probability, stage_type) and the
single number both sides must produce for it. `null` means the column is
NULL / the field is absent, which is a distinct case from 0 on three of
these rows and is the case most of the live board is in.

rows.name: the deal's own probability wins over the stage's
a NULL deal probability inherits the stage default
a stated 0 is a measurement, not a missing value
a deal with no amount forecasts nothing
neither the deal nor the stage says: zero, not an error
a zero amount is zero however sure anybody is
an inherited stage default on an ongoing lane
an override that disagrees with a high stage prior
a small deal on an early lane
a won lane forecasts nothing — that is booked revenue
on_hold is excluded too — the fifth type the prose never mentions
an on_hold deal that would otherwise be the biggest forecast
